finding: Same hormone levels in women who feel awful vs fine; the difference is brain sensitivity to normal shifts (~56% heritable)
plain: Your hormones are completely normal. The difference is how strongly your brain feels the shift.

finding: Calcium ~1000-1200mg/day: 73% fewer symptoms vs 15% placebo (crossover RCT)
plain: Calcium every day, all cycle, is one of the few things with real trial evidence behind it.

finding: hs-CRP >3 linked to 4 of 5 symptom clusters (SWAN, n≈2,900)
plain: Low-grade inflammation tracks with worse weeks.

finding: Cellular (erythrocyte) magnesium lower in PMS even when serum looks normal
plain: Magnesium can run low inside your cells even when a blood test looks fine.

finding: Up to ~46% of women with ADHD report PMDD; dopamine dip is the bridge; adolescent PMS-ADHD OR 2.43
plain: If you have ADHD, the week before your period can hit focus and motivation harder. That's the dopamine dip, not you slacking.

finding: PME (depression/anxiety/bipolar worsening premenstrually) vs true PMDD (clears in follicular phase)
plain: If the heavy feeling never fully lifts after your period, that's worth a proper look.

finding: Cold on the face triggers the diving reflex: heart rate starts dropping within about 10 seconds and vagal activity rises while the cold is on (meta-analysis, 17 studies, 311 people)
plain: Cold water on your face slows your heart within seconds. It lasts about as long as the cold does.

finding: Higher childhood adversity -> stronger premenstrual mood worsening + altered late-luteal cortisol
plain: If your body learned early that the world isn't safe, these weeks can land harder.

finding: Stable blood sugar tracks with steadier mood; PMS linked to glucose/insulin/HOMA-IR differences (mixed)
plain: Eating something steady every few hours keeps your mood from spiking and crashing.

finding: PCOS doesn't cause classic PMS (needs ovulation) but overlaps: insulin resistance + androgens drive mood/cravings
plain: PCOS and PMS aren't the same thing, but they can feed each other.

finding: The ovary is directly wired to the nervous system; nerve signals help regulate ovarian function and fertility decline
plain: Your ovaries and your nervous system are directly wired together.

finding: Chronic psychological stress impairs ovarian function via HPA/cortisol pathways (review)
plain: Ongoing stress doesn't just sit in your head, it can reach your ovaries.

finding: Progressive muscle relaxation reduces PMS symptoms (RCT, 2024)
plain: Tensing and releasing your muscles one group at a time measurably eases PMS.

finding: Cortisol / HPA-axis reactivity shifts across menstrual cycle phases (meta-analysis)
plain: Your stress-hormone response genuinely changes across your cycle.

finding: Add-back paradigm ties symptoms to GABA / allopregnanolone (progesterone metabolite) withdrawal
plain: The calm chemical your body makes from progesterone drops before your period, and sensitive brains feel that withdrawal.

finding: GWAS: premenstrual symptom heritability ~35-57%
plain: A big part of how strongly you feel this is inherited.

finding: Cellular Ca2+/ER-stress + brain-blood-flow studies support the ESC/E(Z) sensitivity finding
plain: Researchers can see the difference in your actual cells and blood flow.

finding: Review: luteal estrogen drop lowers serotonin; reduced allopregnanolone sensitivity -> GABA/glutamate imbalance + HPA activation
plain: When estrogen dips after you ovulate, serotonin dips with it, and your calm system gets thrown off.

finding: Review: neuroinflammation + stressors in PMS/PMDD
plain: Stress and inflammation both feed the premenstrual dip.

finding: Cytokine levels track menstrual symptom severity
plain: Higher inflammation markers line up with worse symptoms.

finding: Vitamin D RCT: supplementation improved symptoms + inflammation markers (in deficiency)
plain: If your vitamin D is low, topping it up may ease things, partly through inflammation.

finding: Melatonin rhythm shifts in PMDD; small interventional melatonin studies show benefit
plain: Your sleep-timing hormone can run off-schedule before your period.

finding: Thyroid dysfunction can mimic PMS (1986 finding; 1990 study failed to replicate)
plain: Thyroid issues can look like PMS, so they're worth ruling out.

finding: Clinical overview of PMS: definition, prevalence, diagnostic criteria, management (StatPearls)
plain: Premenstrual symptoms are a recognized medical condition, not something you're imagining.

finding: Study of whether/why women seek help for menstrual-cycle mental health symptoms
plain: Most women wait a long time before asking for help with this, and that's not a personal failing.

finding: Clinical guide to recognizing and treating PMDD (SSRIs, hormonal options, lifestyle)
plain: There are real, proven treatments for PMDD; knowing them helps you ask for the right help.

finding: Cold water on the face is a standard DBT crisis skill (TIPP). Two small studies found lower heart rate and less self-reported panic, one of them found no change in mood, and no trial has tested the skill on its own
plain: Whether cold actually ends a panic spiral has only been tested on about 30 people at a time.
source: Kyriakoulis et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry 2021
